business.body:
- Part of the Lalbhai Group, described in the deck as 'A USD 3 BILLION DIVERSIFIED ENTERPRISE' across Fashion and Retail, Engineering and Real Estate, with a legacy tracing to 1897 and Arvind Mill (1931) since demerged into four listed entities; Anup is the group's engineering arm, a 'Manufacturer of static state and rotary equipment in heavy engineering segment'.
- '62 YEARS OF EXPERIENCE (ESTABLISHED IN 1962)'; a listed company on BSE & NSE and 'A net debt free company', with annual sales in FY26 of Rs 822 Cr.
- Deck states the company booked orders of more than Rs 150 Cr for Thermal Power plants, 'entering in to elite group of manufacturers of Critical Heat-Exchangers for the sector, which is expected to see significant growth in near future'.
- Licensee positions held for three technologies: Germany polymerization reactors, Italy EM baffle heat exchangers, and Netherlands Helixchangers.
- Serves ten listed industries: oil & gas, fertilizer, specialty chemicals, water/wastewater, refinery, LNG, hydrogen, petrochemicals, power and nuclear.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Strategic stance] For FY27 'the focus of the company this year will be more on Stabilization of current operations, better Execution, Consolidation and Risk mitigation'; on the quarter's shortfall the deck says 'Despite challenges on growth front, we chose to wait out, protecting profitability over short term growth.'
- [Order booking] 'Highest ever order booking during the quarter of ~Rs 315 Cr leading to best pending orderbook visibility (including LOI) of Rs 985 Cr.'
- [Certification breadth] Engineering capability is presented as compliance across ASME Sec I and Sec VIII Div. I & II, EN 13445/PED, GOST R/TRCU, IBR, TEMA/API, AD-2000 Merkblatt HP0, CRN (Canada), ARH (Algeria), SAS (South Africa), NR 13 (Brazil), AS (Australia) and DOSH (Malaysia).
- [Design toolchain] In-house design capability in thermal & mechanical design, vibration analysis, FEA and 3D modelling, using HTRI (Xist & X Vib, Version 8 SP3), ANSYS 18 & NozzlePRO, PVElite, Autopipe (Microprotol), PDS (Inventor), 3D PV and AutoCAD.

deepdive.thesis: Anup Engineering is executing a strategic transformation from a domestic heat exchanger specialist to a diversified process equipment manufacturer with expanded capacity at Kheda, targeting higher-margin exotic metallurgy and export markets, despite near-term margin pressure from raw material spikes. The company is poised for 25%+ CAGR over 3 years, supported by a robust order book and a new facility designed for complex, high-value equipment.

risks.note: The MD&A 'Threats' paragraph names the evolving geopolitical landscape, ongoing regional conflicts, supply chain disruptions and uncertainties from global trade policies and tariff regimes as challenges 'for manufacturers with significant export and import exposure', potentially affecting project execution timelines, material availability, logistics costs and overall operations. This is not theoretical for Anup: the MD & CEO records that in the last few weeks of FY26 critical materials 'not finding ways' and curtailed industrial gas supply restricted the pace of manufacturing, and that a sizeable accumulation of finished goods due to non-availability of shipping lines limited shop-floor flow and impacted progress of new work.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict, sea-route closure and trade/tariff regimes hitting an export-heavy order book

risks.note: The MD & CEO cites volatility in raw material pricing especially steel, energy prices and higher logistics costs, and states the Company will be 'very judicious in booking new orders considering the current high input costs'. With average execution cycles of 12-14 months on large complex projects, input-cost movement between quotation and delivery is a structural margin risk; management also flags that labour, freight and royalty will remain relatively higher in the new order mix.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility (especially steel) and elevated input costs on long-cycle fixed-price orders

risks.note: Explicitly flagged in MD&A 'Threats': the business involves the design and manufacture of highly engineered, custom-built equipment, 'making the availability of a skilled workforce a critical success factor', and the industry continues to face challenges attracting and retaining skilled operators and technical personnel required to support growing demand. Mitigation stated is automation, digitalisation and productivity improvement plus workforce development.
risks.risk: Availability of skilled operators and technical personnel

risks.note: Management states that with the large-sized Kheda facility fully operational the Company is focused on taking large-sized complex projects with long execution cycles (average 12-14 months), so 'it is natural that you will see fluctuations in quarter-on-quarter numbers'. Execution slippage is already visible: the MD notes Mabel's contribution 'would have been better if not for some site projects which got prolonged than expected due to technical changes'. First-time entries into Nuclear, Thermal Power, Clean Energy Storage, Skids and Air Cooled Heat Exchangers add first-of-a-kind execution risk.
risks.risk: Execution risk and earnings lumpiness from large, complex, long-cycle projects

risks.note: BRSR item 19 discloses exports at 48.2% of total turnover in the reporting year, across 12 countries and 13 Indian states, and the MD states the export:domestic ratio continued at 50:50 as a matter of strategic intent. Roughly half of turnover is therefore exposed to cross-border logistics, tariff regimes, currency and the Middle East demand cycle that the MD&A identifies as the key export opportunity.

BRSR discloses one business activity - 'Fabrication of metal and metal products' - at 99.87% of turnover, and one product line (Heat Exchanger, Pressure Vessels, Towers, Reactors, Column and Centrifuges, NIC 28230) also at 99.87%. Within that, Shell & Tube Heat Exchangers have historically been approximately 70% of annual revenue, projected to moderate to approximately 60% in the current year - i.e. diversification is under way but concentration remains high.

Demand is a derived function of capex by Oil & Gas, Petrochemicals, Fertilisers, Hydrogen, Power and LNG customers; MD&A explicitly grounds the outlook in 'healthy capital expenditure across key end-user industries' and 'significant greenfield and brownfield investments'. A capex pause in these industries, or a faster-than-expected transition away from Oil & Gas, transmits directly to order inflow.
risks.risk: End-market cyclicality - dependence on process-industry capital expenditure

risks.note: BRSR Principle 3 reports 13 total recordable work-related injuries to workers in FY 2025-26 (6 in FY 2024-25) and one worker fatality in FY 2024-25 (none in FY 2025-26), while Lost Time Injury Frequency Rate is reported as 0 for both employees and workers in both years - an internal inconsistency worth noting. Of the 13 affected workers in FY26 and 6 in FY25, the number rehabilitated or placed in suitable employment is reported as 0. The workforce structure concentrates this risk: 0 permanent workers versus 783 other-than-permanent workers (100% male) against 391 permanent employees.
risks.risk: Worker safety exposure in a contract-labour-heavy fabrication workforce

meta.thesis: Anup Engineering is executing a strategic transformation from a domestic heat exchanger specialist to a diversified process equipment manufacturer with expanded capacity at Kheda, targeting higher-margin exotic metallurgy and export markets, despite near-term margin pressure from raw material spikes. The company is poised for 25%+ CAGR over 3 years, supported by a robust order book and a new facility designed for complex, high-value equipment.
